transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-10-05 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Leah (Redwood CSM); Jordan, Priya, Samir (NexaHealth)
Recording link: https://redwood.zoom/rec/abc123 (shared)
---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: onboarding status, infra access, early perf results, and then next steps. is the timing still good for 45?
[00:08] Jordan: yeah this is good, thanks Maya. Priya had to hop on late but she's here.
[00:12] Priya: hi all, sorry running a tad behind.
[00:15] Maya: no worries. Samir, can you give a quick update on VPC peering and network?
[00:22] Samir: sure, so we started peering yesterday, the route table entries are half in. we still need the final CIDR confirmation from Redwood side, and we're waiting on the firewall team to allow the outbound on 443 and 8443.
[00:32] Carlos: ok noted, the CIDR is the redwood-public-eips range we shared in the runbook, i'll re-send that doc. the 8443 is used for internal health checks, 443 for the control plane.
[00:40] Jordan: one other blocker is KMS. we generate customer-managed keys for encryption in flight and at rest, but we need to know the exact ARN pattern to grant access.
[00:49] Maya: yep, understood. we'll put the KMS ARN example in the runbook and make it explicit - sorry if that was ambiguous.
[00:54] Samir: also we had an issue with the service account - the token exchange step failed when we tried the initial smoke test. it looks like the IAM policy was missing sts:AssumeRole for the Redwood sidecar.
[01:05] Carlos: ah thanks, that's a common one. in practice you need to add the trust relationship we include in the template. i'll paste a snippet after the call.
[01:13] Priya: for compliance, can you confirm SOC 2 scopes and audit logs retention? we have an internal req for 12 months of immutable logs.
[01:21] Leah: we are SOC 2 compliant and we can offer audit log retention as an add-on; default retention is 90 days but we can extend to 12 months with the compliance package. we'll attach the SOC 2 summary in the drop.
[01:30] Jordan: great. moving to perf: Carlos, you ran the first pass tests yesterday - what did you see?
[01:36] Carlos: yep. quick caveat, these were small synthetic runs against the hosted sandbox. observed roughly p50 110ms, p95 ~320ms for single-shot generation on the smaller open model (we used oak-vic small) - note transcription may mis-label the model name. cost per 1k tokens was about $0.55 on those configs.
[01:55] Jordan: ok that p95 is higher than we'd like for customer-facing endpoints. our SLO is p95 < 250ms.
[02:02] Carlos: understood. two knobs to tighten: reduce max tokens and enable prefix/KV caching for common prompts, and also try the quantized variant on the dedicated pool. on Redwood Dedicate we saw a 30% lower token cost but the latency was similar unless we adjust batching.
[02:18] Priya: can you explain batching tradeoffs? we want low latency but also to not blow cost.
[02:23] Carlos: sure — smaller batches reduce queuing so latency improves but unit cost rises. we can use dynamic batching + latency SLO so the runtime will send small batches during low concurrency and increase batch size when throughput is higher. also prefix caching helps a lot for prompt-heavy workloads.
[02:38] Jordan: any quick wins we can do before dedicated is ready?
[02:42] Maya: yes - enable prefix caching and prompt templating; also try model quantization recommended by Carlos; both are low-effort config changes. we'll provide step-by-step.
[02:51] Samir: on the service account issue, after adding the sts:AssumeRole trust we've had the token step succeed locally, i'll retest with the peered network once routes are in.
[03:01] Carlos: perfect. to add detail: for the p50/p95 numbers i mentioned, we were running concurrency of 8-12 workers, seq length ~256. if you expect longer contexts that'll change the numbers a lot.
[03:14] Priya: our main customer flows are usually 128-256 tokens, but some diagnostic flows hit 1024 occasionally.
[03:21] Carlos: ok then keep an eye on tail latencies for the longer context. we can set up a test to simulate those spikes.
[03:28] Jordan: any security concerns with prefix caching? we have PHI in prompts so we need to be careful.
[03:34] Leah: good point. prefix caching can be configured to be per-tenant and encrypted; with customer-managed KMS you retain control of keys. we'll outline safe configs in the security packet.
[03:44] Maya: quick note on legal/procurement: are you tracking procurement timeline? Jordan?
[03:48] Jordan: procurement kickoff is next week internally, but our legal wants an indemnity clause for data residency. can you share the standard terms?
[03:55] Maya: yes, i'll include the standard enterprise T&C and highlight the provisions we can accept.
[03:59] Priya: regarding metrics, can Redwood expose token-level cost and per-route dashboards into our datadog? we want the same telemetry.
[04:07] Carlos: we have datadog export hooks and can send request traces and metrics; we typically push via a secure forwarder or a cloudwatch->datadog pipeline. we'll include example dashboards.
[04:16] Samir: small note - when you said p50 110ms earlier, was that end-to-end or just inference time?
[04:21] Carlos: that was server-side inference only; end-to-end including network and client will add ~30-60ms depending on peering.
[04:29] Jordan: alright. next, a bit about expected traffic. we anticipate bursty traffic up to 250 RPS during marketing spikes. suggestions?
[04:37] Carlos: for bursty loads, Dedicated with burst capacity is recommended; autoscaling policies and warm pools help. for the POC we can set autoscale thresholds low to simulate bursts without full commit.
[04:48] Priya: cost question - what does a small dedicated pool look like price-wise?
[04:52] Maya: i'll send a rough quote but ballpark for a small reserved pool it's a monthly commit in the tens of thousands depending on GPU class; for POC you can use hosted with burst to simulate.
[05:02] Jordan: ok understood. any blockers on Redwood side to get us to the infra validation?
[05:07] Maya: nothing major — we need the KMS ARN and service account permissions and confirmation when peering routes are live. once those are in we'll run the infra validation.
[05:15] Samir: timeline-wise we should have peering and IAM done by Friday if firewall approves today.
[05:21] Carlos: great. i'll prepare the infra validation checklist and share steps to run the p50/p95 harness.
[05:27] Jordan: one more thing - we ran a tiny functional test and observed occasional 500 errors with the sandbox. could be transient. any known issues?
[05:35] Carlos: there was a config drift in sandbox last week but it should be fixed; if you still see it after peering please capture the request id and we'll trace it.
[05:44] Priya: ok we'll capture logs.
[05:47] Maya: wrapping up then — recap of next steps: Maya sends runbook + security docs, Jordan shares KMS & service account, Samir finishes peering, Carlos prepares validation harness. schedule follow-up infra validation next week.
[05:59] Jordan: thanks all. we'll keep you posted.
---
Notes: transcript includes typical ASR artifacts, occasional mislabels of product names ("Redwood Dedicate" etc.). References to docs: onboarding runbook link (shared in chat), security packet (to be sent).
